request: Our /var/log/nginx/access.log uses the standard combined format. Show the 10 most frequent client IP addresses for responses with status 404, including counts. Also show the first 20 entries with status 500.

steps.task: Show the 10 most frequent client IP addresses and their counts for status 404 in the standard combined-format /var/log/nginx/access.log, ordered by decreasing count.

request: /var/log/myapp/app.log has one entry per line in the format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS LEVEL message. For 2026-06-08, show the 5 most frequent ERROR messages with counts, count ERROR entries by hour in chronological order, and show the last 15 ERROR entries containing the literal text timeout.

steps.command: awk '$1 == "2026-06-08" && $3 == "ERROR" {sub(/^[^ ]+ [^ ]+ [^ ]+ /, ""); count[$0]++} END {for (message in count) print count[message], message}' /var/log/myapp/app.log | sort -k1,1nr | head -n 5

steps.task: Count ERROR entries by hour for 2026-06-08 in /var/log/myapp/app.log, whose entries have the format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS LEVEL message, and display hours in chronological order.
steps.command: awk '$1 == "2026-06-08" && $3 == "ERROR" {count[substr($2, 1, 2)]++} END {for (hour in count) print hour, count[hour]}' /var/log/myapp/app.log | sort -k1,1

request: I'm investigating nginx failures. In the standard combined-format /var/log/nginx/access.log, restrict everything to 08/Jun/2026 and response statuses 500-599: show the first 20 matching entries, the 10 most frequent client IP addresses with counts, the 5 most frequent request paths with counts, and counts by hour in chronological order. steps.command: awk 'index($4, "[08/Jun/2026:") == 1 && $9 >= 500 && $9 <= 599 {count[$1]++} END {for (ip in count) print count[ip], ip}' /var/log/nginx/access.log | sort -k1,1nr -k2,2 | head -n 10

steps.task: Show the 5 most frequent request paths with counts for entries dated 08/Jun/2026 with response statuses 500-599 in the standard combined-format /var/log/nginx/access.log, ordered by decreasing count.
steps.command: awk 'index($4, "[08/Jun/2026:") == 1 && $9 >= 500 && $9 <= 599 {count[$7]++} END {for (path in count) print count[path], path}' /var/log/nginx/access.log | sort -k1,1nr -k2,2 | head -n 5

steps.task: Count entries by hour in chronological order for 08/Jun/2026 with response statuses 500-599 in the standard combined-format /var/log/nginx/access.log.
steps.command: awk 'index($4, "[08/Jun/2026:") == 1 && $9 >= 500 && $9 <= 599 {count[substr($4, 14, 2)]++} END {for (hour in count) print hour, count[hour]}' /var/log/nginx/access.log | sort -k1,1
